answers.answer: In 3 players, a tied lead earns no coin; the lone last player pays 1 coin. In a 2-player unequal Census, the unique leader gains 1 coin, but the last player never pays.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure — Census: unique leader gains; tied lead no coin; unique last pays; 2-player last never pays.

answers.answer: No. Draw any number up to allowance, limited by free Market spaces, so at most two here. Unused Market Followers remain between rounds and occupy capacity.

You may fill an action gradually over multiple rounds. It cannot be executed until all required spaces are occupied by Followers or legal Technology, but a full activation may be saved for a later round. When executed, ordinary-action Followers return to your bag; Technology stays on its spaces.

Starting with Start Player and going clockwise repeatedly, players take one activated action or pass per turn. Passing ends your participation for that Action Phase, so you cannot act again that round; unused activations keep their Followers on the board for future rounds.
Farm House recruits a Farmer into your bag, advances the Farmers Track one space, and gives the good depicted there.

Village recruits one Boatman, Craftsman, or Trader into your bag and advances that profession's track one space. Boatman gives the depicted coins (or a Citizen to the first player at the last space); Craftsman gives a Technology tile; Trader gives a Place Tile (first advance category I only, later I or II).

No: Craftsman Technology is used only after you pass, so it cannot help another action this round after that pass. Your first Technology must replace a Farmer. Each Technology permanently fills one required space, later ones may replace any profession except Monk; never more than one per Place or at a Place requiring only one Follower, and it cannot be moved.
No. The first Trader-track advance allows category I only; each later advance allows I or II. Players may inspect the stacks at any time.

University recruits a Scholar into your bag, advances Scholars Track one space, and grants its depicted Development Points. Castle recruits a Knight into your bag and advances Knights Track; the fourth Knight keeps allowance at 7 and gives its Citizen to the first player there. Monastery recruits a Monk into your bag with no extra track reward. At a track's last space, you cannot take that corresponding action again.
Yes, a Monk may replace a Knight on an ordinary action. No Knight or Technology can replace a required Monk. No, substitutions cannot replace exact professions on Beneficial Deeds.
answers.evidence: Monks; Technology; Town Hall and Beneficial Deeds.

answers.answer: A Ship moves the Merchant one adjacent Waterway connection; a Wagon moves one adjacent Road connection. You may take at most one good from that connection, choosing one if several lie there. Empty connections are legal and yield no good.
Guildhall builds one Trading Station in the Merchant's current town. A town with any player's station cannot receive another, except Orléans, where each player may build one station.

Scriptorium gains 1 Development Point (move one space on the Development Track). Moving onto or past a coin space collects its coins; the first player onto/past a Citizen space collects that Citizen; reaching/passing a Development Status space immediately changes Status to its shown value.
answers.evidence: Actions table — Scriptorium; Scoring / Victory Conditions.

answers.answer: Town Hall works with one or two eligible Followers; starting colored Followers may not enter it. Send one or both to free Beneficial Deed spaces matching their exact professions, possibly on different Deeds. Each placement earns the depicted 1, 2, or 3 coins; Canalization gives a choice of 1 coin or 1 Development Point. The player filling a Deed's last space takes its Citizen.
answers.evidence: Actions — Town Hall and Beneficial Deeds; Planning states one space is enough.

answers.answer: Pilgrimage prohibits Monk recruitment during Phase 5 (Actions); it already applies before the Event Phase. Other events resolve in Phase 6. Round 1 opens with Pilgrimage because that tile is placed on top of the Hour Glass stack.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure — Hour Glass and Event; Setup step 4.

answers.answer: Only grain, cheese, or wine count as food; wool does not. Paid food goes to the Goods Market. If unable to pay food, you owe 5 coins; with fewer than five coins, pay what you have and undergo torture for each missing coin.

The neutral Scholar returns to its game-board supply and is recruitable again; its track marker does not move back. A drawn marked starting Trader is kept, with no Follower lost and no redraw. Starting Followers cannot be lost to Plague.
answers.evidence: Events — Plague; Torture states marked starting Followers always stay.

answers.answer: Pay the one available coin, then replace each of the two missing coins with one eligible item: a built or unbuilt Trading Station, random eligible neutral Follower from your bag, one Development Point, one Goods Tile, Place Tile, or Technology tile. For Followers, redraw marked starters until a neutral one; marked starters always stay. A Development Point moves one space left but never onto or past a coin space. Surrendered items are removed from the game; only lost Development Points can be regained.

You cannot play an action that provides an unavailable Character, Technology, or Goods tile, even if another part would still reward you. It becomes available again when the required tile returns to stock, subject to normal requirements. If the common coin supply is insufficient, players cannot receive coins at that moment.

A tie for most built stations awards the remaining Citizen to nobody. Goods score grain 1, cheese 2, wine 3, wool 4, brocade 5 each. Stations and collected Citizens score (built stations + Citizens) × final Development Status. Highest total wins; ties go to the player furthest ahead on Development Track, then are shared if still tied.

Each player takes a board, bag, Merchant, 10 stations, 5 coins, 7 markers, and four marked starting Followers. Put starting Followers on the Market, Merchant in Orléans, and one marker on the first space of each of six Character Tracks and the Development Track. Keep coins and unbuilt stations in front of you. The youngest player takes Start Player token.

Place 13 Citizens on their marked board/Deed spaces and set the remaining Citizen aside for the final Trading Station award. Sort neutral Followers by profession into their buildings, Technology into its supply, and coins nearby. Separate Place Tiles into categories I and II; players may inspect stacks. Shuffle goods and place one face up on each eligible Road/Waterway goods space; in a 4-player game fill every such space. Sort remaining goods face up into Goods Market.

For 3 players remove 2 neutral Farmers, Boatmen, Craftsmen, and Traders each; 3 neutral Knights, Scholars, and Monks each; 6 random goods; leave spaces marked 4 empty. For 2 players remove 4 of each of the first four professions; 6 of each Knight, Scholar, and Monk; 12 random goods; leave spaces marked 3 or 4 empty. Remove all starting Followers of unused colors.
answers.evidence: Setup — Fewer players table and preceding sentence.

answers.answer: Farm House: Boatman + Craftsman. Village: Farmer + Boatman + Craftsman. University: Farmer + Craftsman + Trader. Castle: Farmer + Boatman + Trader. Monastery: Scholar + Trader.
Ship: Farmer + Boatman + Knight. Wagon: Farmer + Trader + Knight. Guildhall: Farmer + Craftsman + Knight.

Scriptorium requires Knight + Scholar. Town Hall permits one or two eligible Followers; their exact professions are not restricted in the summary's action table, but marked starting Followers may not enter Town Hall.
answers.evidence: Actions table; Town Hall and Beneficial Deeds.

answers.answer: Yes. For each declined draw, you may instead move one Follower from an Action Space back to your Market. You may not move one directly from one Action Space to another.
Yes. You may inspect your bag at any time, but shuffle its contents afterward.

Hour Glass, Census, Followers, Planning, Actions, Event, Start Player. Pass Start Player to the player on your left. Planning begins simultaneously; announce completion, and if order matters plan clockwise from Start Player. Event payments and other necessary order-sensitive resolutions proceed clockwise from Start Player. Paid coins go to the common supply; received coins come from it.
Finish the entire round in which the 18th tile is drawn, including its event; scoring is after that.
The uniquely ahead player on the Farmers Track gains the Census coin, regardless of Farmer tiles in bags.
Income pays coins equal to current Development Status.
Eight goods means two complete groups of three, so pay 2 coins; types do not affect the count. A shortfall causes torture.
answers.evidence: Events — Taxes: count all goods, 1 coin per complete group of 3 (round down); shortfall causes torture.

answers.answer: You receive 4 coins; only built Trading Stations count for Trading Day, not the six unbuilt ones.
answers.evidence: Events — Trading Day; Building says only built stations count for income and scoring.

answers.answer: Hayrick: Farmer, 1 grain; Cheese Factory: Farmer + Farmer, 1 cheese; Winery: Farmer + Trader, 1 wine; Wool Manufacturer: Boatman + Trader, 1 wool; Tailor Shop: Scholar + Trader, 1 brocade. Each takes the good from the Goods Market and cannot be used if that particular good is absent there.
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles; final goods-producing Place sentence.

answers.answer: Shipping Line: Boatman, gain 1 Development Point. Brewery: Monk, gain 2 coins. Windmill: Craftsman + Craftsman, gain 2 coins and 1 Development Point. Library: Knight + Scholar, gain 2 Development Points.
Any one Follower activates Pharmacy. Pay 1–3 coins and advance one Development space per coin; paying two advances two spaces. Zero and four coins are not legal.
Cellar: Monk + Scholar, gain 4 coins. Office: Scholar + Scholar, gain 1 coin per built Trading Station. Hospital: Boatman + Scholar, gain coins equal to current Development Status.
Horse Wagon requires Trader + Knight. It moves along one Road to an adjacent town and collects one good if available.
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles — Horse Wagon.

answers.answer: Laboratory requires Scholar + Craftsman and gives a Technology tile. It can be placed on itself if legal: your first-ever Technology may go there only if replacing a Farmer; a later one may go there if no Technology is already there and other placement limits are met.
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles — Laboratory; Technology.

answers.answer: Bathhouse requires a Farmer. Draw three Followers from your bag, choose two, and immediately place them on appropriate Action Spaces; neither may go on Bathhouse. Return the third drawn Follower and the activating Bathhouse Farmer to your bag.

Place the one legally placeable drawn Follower on an appropriate Action Space other than Bathhouse. Return the other two drawn Followers and the activating Farmer to your bag. If none can be placed, return all three drawn Followers and the activating Farmer to your bag.
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles — Bathhouse: if only one or none can be placed, do so and return all other drawn Followers to the bag; also return activating Follower.

answers.answer: It may be executed on a later action turn this round, provided you have not passed; actions may be chosen freely and a player alternates taking actions until passing.
answers.evidence: Actions phase: one activated action or passing per turn; choose order freely. Planning describes activation and saved actions.

answers.answer: Sacristy requires a Monk. If activated, during Phase 6 it protects against a negative event such as Harvest, Taxes, or Plague; return its Monk to your bag instead of suffering the event.
No. Pilgrimage prohibits Monk recruitment during Phase 5, before Phase 6 when Sacristy's event protection is used, so Sacristy does not override the prohibition.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure — Hour Glass; Events — Pilgrimage; Sacristy.

answers.answer: Herb Garden lets Boatmen replace Craftsmen, Traders, and Farmers on ordinary actions. It does not let them replace Knights, Scholars, or Monks.
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles — Herb Garden.

answers.answer: School lets Scholars replace other professions except Monks on ordinary actions. It requires no activation. A Scholar cannot replace a required Monk.
No. Beneficial Deeds require exact professions, and substitutions cannot replace the professions depicted there. Using Gunpowder Tower does not change the exact-type requirement.
answers.evidence: Town Hall and Beneficial Deeds; Gunpowder Tower.

answers.answer: Gunpowder Tower adds 2 Market spaces. During Phase 3 place 1 or 2 drawn Followers there; during Planning move one or both to Action Spaces, or during Actions send one or both directly to Beneficial Deeds in a single action. Marked starting Followers cannot be sent, and Deeds still require exact types.
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles — Gunpowder Tower.

answers.answer: The unique leader gains 1 coin; neither tied-last player pays, because a tied last place pays nothing.

The unique leader in built Trading Stations takes the set-aside Citizen before scoring, after the whole final round including its event. The collected Citizen counts in final scoring as part of Citizens.
Remove the lighter Pilgrimage tile, shuffle the other 17 Hour Glass tiles face down, then place Pilgrimage on top. In Phase 1 the Start Player reveals the top tile.
answers.evidence: Setup step 4; Turn Structure — Hour Glass.

answers.answer: Each remaining coin scores 1 victory point.
Development Status starts at 1 and initial Knight-track draw allowance is 4.
Only lost Development Points can be regained. Surrendered goods, Followers, stations, Places, and Technology are removed from the game, not returned to supplies.
You may choose your actions' order freely.
The summary does not specify whether the passive substitution ability becomes available immediately upon acquiring Herb Garden or School during the Action Phase. This timing detail is unsupported.
answers.evidence: Place Tiles says they give ongoing abilities; no acquisition-timing rule stated.

answers.answer: You may send just one; Town Hall accepts one or both Followers in one action.
answers.evidence: Town Hall and Beneficial Deeds: send one or both.

answers.answer: Taking a good is optional: you may take one good from the connection, choosing one if several lie there, or leave it. The summary does not state this as a separate explicit ruling, but “may take one” makes it optional.
answers.evidence: Movement and goods: “You may take one good from that connection, choosing one if several lie there.”

answers.answer: Yes. You may send the second on a later action turn in the same Action Phase before passing; Town Hall may resolve its two Followers in the same or separate actions.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings; Actions phase passing rule.
